attack.falsification_criterion: REFUTED if, for ANY (hardener, literature reactivity ratio) combination, amine-starved MC sol fraction is NOT strictly greater than amine-rich MC sol fraction.
attack.hypothesis_H2_reactivity_robust: The H2 direction rule (amine-starved sol strictly greater than amine-rich sol at equal-magnitude +-30% stoichiometric offset, for every g>f marine-primer pair) continues to hold when the equal-group-reactivity idealisation is replaced by the literature-measured primary/secondary amine-H rate ratio.

does_not_close: PHASE_1_INDEPENDENT_EVALUATION (needs an external measured sol-fraction / extractables reference set; none rights-clean in the portfolio)
external_rights (fixture is self-authored CC0; the reactivity ratios are from a published peer-reviewed source cited above, not portfolio data)
pre_existing_secondary_amine_hardeners (DETA/TETA and similar polyamines with a structurally secondary N already present unreacted; needs a 3-state-per-molecule MC model, not attempted here)
temperature_dependence_of_r (Girard-Reydet et al. report r as roughly constant over their studied cure temperature range for a given diamine, but the portfolio has not pinned r(T) generally)

cyclization_magnitude (this MC does not reject intra-cluster bonds, unlike the prior receipt's analytic idealisation, so absolute sol-fraction magnitudes are not expected to match the analytic model exactly except at the validated equal-reactivity control; only the DIRECTION rule is being tested)
kinetic_gel_time (thermodynamic/topological gel-point conversion only, no rate law integrated over time)
excluded_hardeners_reason: carry at least one structurally secondary amine N-H already present in the unreacted molecule (e.g. DETA/TETA internal -NH-); the 2-primary-site/4H MC model does not represent them. A pre-existing-secondary-site MC model is a distinct, separately-scoped extension -- logged as does_not_close, not attempted here.
interpretation: RDKit per-atom re-derivation of amine N-site structure agrees with the fixture for all 6 checked records (True). Of the 5 candidate hardeners, 3 (hardener-ipda, hardener-pacm, hardener-mxda) are all-primary (2 N-sites x 2H) and eligible for the 2-primary-site MC model; ['hardener-deta', 'hardener-teta'] are excluded (structurally secondary N already present) and out of scope for this study. Validation gate: MC at the equal-reactivity control (r=1.0, N=20000 resin molecules) reproduces the SIGNED analytic sol_wt_pct from role-macosko-miller-sol-latitude-v1 within tolerance on 9/9 checks (all_pass=True), so the MC methodology is trusted for the attack. Attack: across 6 (hardener x literature reactivity-ratio) combinations spanning r=k2/k1 in {0.65, 0.45} (Girard-Reydet et al. 1995, DGEBA + aromatic diamines), the H2 direction rule holds in 6/6 cases. H2 is CORROBORATED under both literature reactivity ratios for every eligible hardener: introducing the real, measured kinetic substitution effect (secondary amine-H up to 55% less reactive than primary) changes the MAGNITUDE of the starved/rich sol asymmetry but not its SIGN, so the zero-fitted-parameter directional design rule 'err amine-rich, never amine-starved' survives this attack. This closes the equal_reactivity_idealisation gap left open by the prior receipt for the 3 all-primary hardeners tested (IPDA, PACM, MXDA); DETA/TETA and other pre-existing-secondary-amine hardeners remain untested (see does_not_close). AUDIT_ONLY; no candidate, product, objective, manifest edit, or promotion claim.

monte_carlo_model.cyclization_policy: intra-cluster bonds are NOT rejected: a finite forest on N_A+N_B nodes has at most N_A+N_B-1 edges, far fewer than required to reach the target conversion, so forbidding them would make the target unreachable. This is the standard random-graph (configuration-model) realisation of Flory-Stockmayer/Macosko-Miller mean-field theory, under which the tree approximation is asymptotically exact pre-gel and intra-cluster bonds are normal post-gel.
monte_carlo_model.determinism: random.Random seeded by int(sha256(run-identifying-string)[:16],16); no wall-clock, no OS entropy, no dict/set iteration order dependence
monte_carlo_model.method: finite-population kinetic Monte Carlo, weighted-union-find connectivity
monte_carlo_model.scope_restriction: restricted to hardeners whose every reactive amine nitrogen is primary (2H) in the unreacted state, verified per-atom via RDKit (not asserted)
monte_carlo_model.stopping_rule: complete conversion of the limiting group (p_A=1 if r>=1 else p_A=r); identical convention to the analytic Study 2 anchor

primary_references: Girard-Reydet, E.; Riccardi, C.C.; Sautereau, H.; Pascault, J.-P. (1995) "Epoxy-Aromatic Diamine Kinetics. Part 1. Modeling and Influence of the Diamine Structure." Macromolecules 28(23):7599-7607. doi:10.1021/ma00127a003
Odian, G. (2004) Principles of Polymerization, 4th ed., Wiley, ch.2, ISBN 978-0-471-27400-1

prior receipt under attack: role-macosko-miller-sol-latitude-v1 (Macosko, C.W.; Miller, D.R. (1976) Macromolecules 9(2):199-206, doi:10.1021/ma60050a003; Miller, D.R.; Macosko, C.W. (1976) Macromolecules 9(2):206-211, doi:10.1021/ma60050a004)
purpose: Falsification attack on the role-macosko-miller-sol-latitude-v1 H2 direction rule ('err amine-rich, never amine-starved') under the literature-measured primary/secondary amine-H kinetic substitution effect (unequal group reactivity), which that receipt explicitly left unmodelled. Independent method: finite-population kinetic Monte Carlo (not the recursive generating-function method), validated against the prior receipt's SIGNED analytic values at the equal-reactivity control before being trusted for the attack.

validation_gate.purpose: MC at the equal-reactivity control (r_ratio=1.0) must reproduce the SIGNED prior receipt's analytic sol_wt_pct values within finite-population Monte Carlo noise before the MC is trusted for the attack.
